title: Introduce alert anchoring and token fidelity shepherd
author: Sofia Martinez
release_notes: Adds an adaptive alert anchoring component that ties alert thresholds to token-fidelity baselines, a lightweight fidelity_shepherd service for per-route drift detection and recommendations, new dashboard panels (fidelity sparkline, anchoring suggestions), and instrumentation to emit token_fidelity_score for traces and logs. Backwards-compatible; runtime emits additional optional tags.
description:
Context: production teams are seeing noisy SLO alerts driven by rare high-cost tokens and prompt-shape oscillations. This PR introduces a two-piece observability feature: 1) alert anchoring — a policy layer that computes per-route, per-tenant baseline windows and suggests threshold adjustments (and can apply auto-proposals for SRE review); and 2) fidelity_shepherd — a small continuous analyzer that monitors token-level fidelity metrics (token_fidelity_score) and surfaces correlated cost/latency drift with a suggested mitigation (canary rollback, increase batching, or quantize model variant).

What changed (high level):
- telemetry: emit token_fidelity_score (0..1) on invocation spans and as a structured log field when available; add token_cost_component tag to span (cpu,gpu,kv_cache).
- fidelity_shepherd service: new microservice in telemetry/ with a simple rule engine that identifies drift windows, computes anchor candidates, and writes proposals to an Anchors API. Runs with low QPS and has a safe read-only mode.
- alert anchoring: added a controller that reads anchor proposals and pairs them with existing SLO rules, exposing an interactive suggestion in the Observability Console.
- dashboards: new dashboard panels (fidelity sparkline, anchored-threshold overlay, drift heatmap) and a compact explainer panel for suggested actions.
- tests: unit tests + integration test harness simulating token-fidelity regressions.

Checklist (checked):
- [x] Emit token_fidelity_score in traces and structured logs (opt-in config flag: telemetry.emit_token_fidelity).
- [x] fidelity_shepherd service with metrics and health endpoints.
- [x] Anchors API and UI panel in console (read-only by default).
- [x] Prometheus recording rules for anchor metrics and Grafana dashboard JSON.
- [x] E2E test that simulates fidelity drop and verifies proposal creation.
- [x] Documentation draft and runbook entries included.

Commits (summary):
- add: token_fidelity_score field to tracer instrumentation (sdk/python and runtime instrumenter).
- feat: fidelity_shepherd service + rule engine + health checks.
- feat: alert anchoring controller + Anchors API.
- ui: console panels for fidelity sparkline and anchoring suggestions.
- infra: recording rules + alertmanager template for anchored alerts.
- test: e2e fidelity regression test harness.

Files changed (selected):
- telemetry/fidelity_shepherd/main.go (new) — shepherd service with rule engine and proposal writer.
- telemetry/proposals/api.go (new) — Anchors API (read/write for proposals, currently RBAC-protected).
- runtime/instrumentation/token_tags.go — emits token_fidelity_score and token_cost_component.
- sdk/python/redwood/telemetry.py — optional helper to compute token_fidelity_score on-client prompt quality hooks.
- console/dashboards/fidelity_sparkline.json — dashboard panels and templated variables.
- monitoring/prometheus/recording_rules_anchor.yml — new recording rules.
- monitoring/alertmanager/anchored_alerts.yml — sample anchored alert templates.
- tests/e2e/fidelity_proposal_test.go — integrates shepherd with telemetry simulator.
- docs/observability/fidelity_shepherd.md — design and runbook.

Testing and CI: initial CI run failed with lint on console JSON (naming convention). Fixes applied in second commit; full CI passed (unit tests, integration harness, lint). Prometheus rules validated with promtool. Load test of fidelity_shepherd done in staging with synthetic traces at 50rps for 20 minutes — shepherd CPU < 1 vCPU and memory stable.

Rollout plan:
- Merge to main behind feature flag (observability.feature_fidelity_shepherd).
- Enable telemetry.emit_token_fidelity default=false; dev tenants opt-in.
- Stage shepherd as read-only and surface UI suggestions to SREs. After 2 weeks of stable data, enable auto-proposals in a canary subset.

Migration notes:
- No db migrations. Anchors API uses existing proposals store (append-only). If telemetry.emit_token_fidelity=false no extra tags are emitted. Older traces remain compatible.

Review conversation (high-level excerpt):
- Asha Patel (reviewer): "Nice end-to-end. Two asks: (1) can the shepherd back off aggressively under high cardinality tenants? (2) please ensure the Anchors API has RBAC checks so only SRE/service owners can apply auto-proposals."
- Author reply (Sofia): "(1) shepherd has tenant backoff rules and a per-tenant sampling cap (configurable). I added unit tests demonstrating backoff. (2) Anchors API enforces RBAC via existing auth middleware; added test coverage."
- Liam O'Connor: "Dashboard looks good; minor comment on color contrast for the heatmap. Also suggest calling out expected cost of running shepherd in the runbook."
- Sofia: "Adjusted palette and added staging cost estimate to runbook (approx. $0.12/hr at 50rps in staging)."
- Marcus Chen: "Left a nit on naming in telemetry tags (token_cost_component -> token_cost_source). I kept current name for now to match historical code; added compatibility mapping in the tracer to accept both tags."
- Marcus (approval): "Looks good after fixes."

Merge outcome: Squash-merged to main after all approvals and passing CI. Release notes added to the changelog and docs updated. Console feature gated behind observability.feature_fidelity_shepherd and telemetry.emit_token_fidelity.

Why this is different: Anchoring ties alert thresholds to real fidelity baselines (not just token counts or raw percentiles) and provides human-readable proposals rather than automatic threshold changes; fidelity_shepherd focuses on surfacing cause (e.g., prompt-shape drift, model variant changes) with low-cost continuous sampling. This complements existing token-cost and latency telemetry by adding a quality-aware observability layer.
